results.hypothesis: To determine whether gradient-boosted decision trees (XGBoost and LightGBM) maintain or improve their accuracy advantage over neural networks as the training set size increases from 1000 to 100,000 records on the UCI Statlog German Credit dataset.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Performance of all models on the original 1000-record dataset
results.success_criteria: Supporting the hypothesis would mean that both XGBoost and LightGBM maintain or improve their accuracy advantage over neural networks as training set size increases. Refuting the hypothesis would occur if neural networks show equal or greater accuracy than GBDTs at larger training set sizes.
results.notes: Neural networks show equal or greater accuracy than GBDTs at larger training set sizes, refuting the hypothesis.

Using a fixed 80/20 train/test split ensures consistent evaluation across all training set sizes
All models are evaluated on the same held-out test set for fair comparison
The experiment assumes that the performance difference observed at larger training set sizes reflects true scaling behavior rather than artifacts of the sampling procedure

reference_implementations.title: When Do Neural Nets Outperform Boosted Trees on Tabular Data?
reference_implementations.tldr: The comparison between neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees on tabular data shows that performance differences are often negligible, and hyperparameter tuning is more crucial than choosing the algorithm. TabPFN outperforms other models on smaller datasets, while GBDTs handle irregular datasets better.

reference_implementations.title: NRGBoost: Energy-Based Generative Boosted Trees
reference_implementations.tldr: Energy-based generative boosting achieves competitive discriminative and generative performance on tabular data, outperforming existing generative approaches and matching neural network performance in sampling.
